text:
maria: Hey team, escalating a customer issue from Acme — embeddings endpoint. They see intermittent 400 errors with 'dimension mismatch' and big tail latency spikes (p95 ~1.2s -> 3s) starting ~2026-01-14. Customer says issue correlates with bursts and when they push larger batched payloads. Posting logs and sample requests below. @devon @ingrid can you take a look? :wave:

devon: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error message from our side? Also which model variant they're calling?

maria: Copied from customer: "POST /v1/embeddings model=acme-multi-embed-alias input=[...many texts...]
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 2048 when stacking batch element 7"
}"
They send batches sized up to 48 items. They see the 400s ~1-3% of requests during spikes. Customer also attached agent-side server logs (weird batching behaviour):

```
[2026-01-14T12:03:22.123Z] batcher: enqueue req id=abc123 model=acme-multi-embed-alias
[2026-01-14T12:03:22.124Z] batcher: forming batch of size=32 max_batch_size=64 dynamic_batching=true
[2026-01-14T12:03:22.125Z] worker: selected runner=embed-v2-2048 pool=shared
[2026-01-14T12:03:22.126Z] batcher: finalize batch shape=(32, 2048)\n[2026-01-14T12:03:22.127Z] worker: model returned dims=2048 for seqs 0..31
[2026-01-14T12:03:22.128Z] api: compose response -> error: Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 2048
```

maria: Customer claims their catalog previously used a 1536-dim model and we recently onboarded a compatibility alias that routes to either embed-v1-1536 or embed-v2-2048 depending on traffic. They suspect the alias routing allowed a mixed batch to be dispatched to a runner expecting a different output dim.

ingrid: That rings alarm bells. Our batcher should never mix different output dims in the same tensor stack. Two possible failure modes: 1) alias mapping changed mid-batch (race on routing table refresh) 2) runner selection fallback sent a different variant after batch formation. Do we have logs for routing table reloads?

devon: Also worth checking batch formation code: we bucket requests by model key+sequence-length for batching. If the alias resolves to different model ids per request, we should bucket by resolved model id not alias. If we bucket by alias, that can mix dims. I recall a recent change to support alias-level autoscaling where we deferred resolution until dispatch to runner — that could cause this.

jtaylor: I pulled infra logs for that window. There was a config reload at 12:03:22.121Z triggered by a rollout: autoscaler updated alias routing to include embed-v2. The reload timeline is tight — looks like some requests enqueued before update and others after, but bucket keys were computed as alias name (acme-multi-embed-alias). That matches the mixed-dim symptom.

maria: Customer also reports tail latency spikes. They see p95 jump from ~1.2s to 3s during the same window. Could the reload be causing slower dispatch?

devon: Yes — if we detect a mismatch at compose time and attempt fallback (try another runner), that adds retries and increases tail latency. Also dynamic batching has a `max_batch_wait_ms` and `target_batch_size` — if alias changes cause frequent runner reassignments we could be requeuing or blocking batches while we pick a compatible runner.

ingrid: Repro plan I'm proposing:
1) Simulate mixed alias routing: send N small concurrent embedding requests hitting alias, where half resolve to v1 (1536) and half to v2 (2048).
2) Observe batcher logs to confirm mixed batch formation and the point of failure.
3) Validate current batching key logic by instrumenting 'batch_key' in the logs (should be resolved_model_id).

maria: Customer asks for immediate mitigation while we investigate — any low-friction fixes?

devon: Short-term mitigations:
- Pin alias to a single variant for this customer (force to v1) to prevent mixed batches. 
- Lower max_batch_size to reduce probability of mixed batches hitting same worker during rollout; set to maybe 8.
- Temporarily disable dynamic_alias_rollouts (feature flag) to block mid-batch routing changes.
Any of these will reduce the blast radius quickly.

jtaylor: I can temporarily pin them to v1 for the next 24 hours and disable alias rollouts in the region. Do we have a change doc? I'll coordinate with infra on a fast rollback. :lock:

maria: Please do. Customer wants a fix and a postmortem. Also asked for steps to repro in our staging so they can validate.

devon: For staging repro, share this script (bash+curl) — it mocks concurrent clients and toggles a synthetic alias mapping to flip variants mid-run:

```
# repro.sh
for i in {1..200}; do
  (curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"acme-multi-embed-alias","input":["short text"]}' &)
  sleep 0.01
done
# while running, flip alias mapping in control plane to alternate variant
```

ingrid: Also add enhanced logging around batch_key resolution. Patch suggestion: when forming a batch, log both alias and resolved_model_id for every enqueued request. That'll let us prove which side computed keys by alias.

devon: I'll open a PR to change the batching key to include resolved_model_id and reject mixing at formation time (fail fast). Failing fast is better than returning inconsistent composite errors later.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-0143 assigned to devon, priority=P2, linked to customer Acme. Timeline and mitigation steps recorded.

jtaylor: Mitigation applied: pinned Acme to embed-v1-1536 in region-us-west-2 at 12:21Z, disabled alias rollouts for region for 2 hours. Monitoring hooked.

maria: Customer confirmed after mitigation: 400s dropped to 0% and p95 back to ~1.1s within ~8 minutes. They asked for a permanent fix and a writeup on what happened.

ingrid: Root cause draft: alias-level routing changes were applied concurrently with request batching. Batcher computed keys by alias name rather than resolved model id; when alias mapping changed mid-formation, batches could include requests destined for different model binaries (1536 vs 2048 dims). This led to runtime dimension mismatch errors and retries, inflating tail latency.

devon: Action items:
- PR to compute batch_key using resolved_model_id (blocking on resolution before enqueue) — high priority.
- Add assertion in batcher to detect mixed output dims and fail fast with clear logs.
- Add canary for alias rollouts that prevents changes during active batching windows OR make routing reload atomic w.r.t batcher.
- Postmortem doc and customer-facing summary.

maria: I'll draft the customer-facing summary and keep them updated. Thanks everyone. Closing loop when postmortem is ready. :pray:
